core_obligations: Reduce to a single class (proof lines 7152-7159): given X in C and F in A_X, take a class xi in H^{n+1}_tau(U, F) over some U/X and aim to show that, after restricting to the members of a tau'-covering, its pullback vanishes.

Use locality and the situation (proof lines 7162-7172): locality of cohomology lets the author choose a tau-covering on which xi restricts to zero, and the data {V_j -> V} of the situation then produce the arrow f : X -> Y of P with {X -> Y} a tau-covering and a class xi in H^{n+1}_tau(Y, F) that dies after pullback to X.

Apply the hypothesis (V_n) (proof lines 7184-7194): the comparison result for degree n produces a unique tau'-class theta in H^{n+1}_{tau'}(X, epsilon_{X,*}F) mapping to xi|_X, and since xi|_X pulls back to zero, theta is the pulled back class, so by (V_n) applied to the relevant data theta dies on a tau'-covering after pullback along an arrow of P.

Finish with the Leray-type computation (proof lines 7197-7289): the assumption that xi maps to zero under F -> Rf_{tau,*}f_tau^{-1}F together with the cited Leray lemma and a distinguished-triangle argument shows that xi itself dies on the members of a tau'-covering after pullback, which is (V_{n+1}).
proof_roadmap: Take an arbitrary class in degree n+1 and aim to kill it locally for the topology tau'.
Use locality of cohomology to replace the object by the target of an arrow of P that is a tau-covering.
Invoke the degree-n comparison to produce the corresponding tau'-class and apply the induction hypothesis (V_n) to it.
Use the hypothesis that the class dies under the adjunction map and the Leray-type lemma to conclude (V_{n+1}).
difficulty_reason: The lemma proves the induction step (V_n) implies (V_{n+1}) in the comparison of two topologies on a site carrying the data of the situation, namely a set of arrows P and weak Serre subcategories A'_X of the tau'-sheaves (statement lines 7147-7150, with the situation delivered verbatim as a context span from lines 6840-6879). The proof has four stages: an arbitrary class in degree n+1 is replaced, using locality of cohomology, by the target of an arrow of P that is a tau-covering (proof lines 7152-7172); the degree-n comparison result produces the corresponding tau'-class and the induction hypothesis kills it locally after pullback along an arrow of P (proof lines 7184-7194); finally the hypothesis that the class dies under the canonical map F -> Rf_{tau,*}f_tau^{-1}F, together with the cited Leray-type lemma and a distinguished-triangle argument, kills the original class on a tau'-covering, which is the assertion (proof lines 7205-7289). The non-formal content is the bookkeeping that lets the degree-n statement be applied to the twisted data and then lifted back. The claim is H2: a long reduction, written out in full, with each step attributed to a named result of the same section.
